text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Education Ministry has invited schools to give their views on how to reform the secondary school system.
- The textiles association rejected a government dispatch on work breaks and said workers were not available for duty during short breaks at the work place.

- EU financing for the Alqueva dam in the Alentejo in southeast Portugal should be available soon after lobbying by President Jorge Sampaio and Foreign Minister Jaime Gama, and confirmation from Spain that the dam would receive enough water.

- The Social Security Ministry has recovered 136 billion escudos in revenues -- more than initial expectations -- under the so-called "Mateus Plan", designed to recover tax and social security arrears from companies.
- The Socialist Party will propose to President Sampaio possible dates for a referendum on the creation of administrative regions in Portugal.
- The Employment Ministry said unemployment fell 0.7 percent in February 1997, compared with February 1996.
- In the spring of 1998, Lisbon stock exchange may adopt the same trading system as that used by Paris bourse, according to a recommendation from consultants Deloitte.
- In July the European Commission will present plans to extend structural funds to EU states beyond 1999.
-- Opel Portugal is planning a new investment in the painting division of its factory at Azambuja, north of Lisbon, its president in Portugal Marc Verschueren told the paper.
